ordered_diagnoses: Squamous cell carcinoma with clear cell features

s1.syndrome_frame: A slowly growing eyelid mass with recent changes and crust formation
salient_findings: Yellowish-brown, well-circumscribed papule on the central lower eyelid
Flakier surface at one lateral end
Hyperkeratotic lesion with pseudohorn cysts and neoplastic squamous cell proliferation
key_facts: 4-year history of a left lower eyelid mass
Recent growth and crust formation
Papule is well-circumscribed and located on the central lower eyelid
Tumor has a flakier surface at one lateral end
Specimen measured 0.8 × 0.5 × 0.3 cm
Hyperkeratotic lesion with many pseudohorn cysts
Proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells
Malignant squamous cells have eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli
Mitotic figures are present
Ki67 staining highlights scattered basal cells and approximately 20-40% of tumor cell nuclei

shortlist: Squamous cell carcinoma with clear cell features

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Malignant squamous cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli, mitotic figures, and Ki67 staining patterns are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Verrucous carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperkeratotic lesion with pseudohorn cysts and well-circumscribed papule are features that can be seen in verrucous carcinoma

shortlist.label: Keratoacanthoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid growth and crust formation, along with the presence of pseudohorn cysts, could suggest keratoacanthoma

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma with clear cell features
shortlist.why_kept: Clear cell change in the central areas, periodic acid-Schiff positive and diastase sensitive, supports this specific variant of squamous cell carcinoma

shortlist.label: Actinic keratosis
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperkeratotic lesion and the location on the eyelid, an area prone to sun exposure, make actinic keratosis a plausible consideration
